subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a static armoured truck model, deciding to skip rigging and joints and build it as grouped parts instead - eight wheels across four axles, a front cab, and an armoured cargo pod behind it.

I'm sketching out the overall dimensions and layout, including chassis frame placement, wheel sizing and positioning per axle, and which texture/paint helpers (glow kit, panelled metal, SVG decals) to use for armor plating, hazard stripes, and other details.

Now I'm detailing the wheel assembly with tread blocks, a rim hub with lug nuts and a neon ring, plus fender guards, before moving to the cab layout with hood and cab box dimensions placed along the z-axis.

Next I'm adding the windshield as a slanted glowing visor plane, roof armor with a colored light bar and turret assembly, a bull-bar front bumper with chevron and headlights, rear exhaust stacks, and side mirrors -- then shifting focus to laying out the pod section behind the cab.

I'm defining the pod's dimensions and building its body as an octagonal-profile extrusion running along the z-axis, giving it a chamfered box shape with panelled paint, rib bands, corner bolts, and sealed rear doors.

I'm adding details like a hazard-striped rear door plane, side cargo labels, glowing amber status lights, a top hatch with a red seal and antennas, plus armor skirt plates with hazard stripes and horizontal fuel tank cylinders positioned between the axles under the frame.

I'm working through the chassis geometry now, checking ground clearance against tank and wheel placement, sizing the chassis box height and wheel positions so they align without overlap, then setting overall vehicle width, cab width, and pod base position relative to the wheel arches before adding fender boxes over the front wheels.

Now I'm adjusting fender dimensions to avoid conflicts with the pod's base position, settling on slightly narrower fender plates even though there's a bit of overlap. I'm also adding a dark deck box beneath the pod, and planning out the textures I'll need: hazard stripes, a visor, a company logo emblem, pod door markings, and side labels.

I'm defining paint materials using panelled metal textures with specific panel sizes and rivet details for the armor, a blued metal finish for the pod, and a mottled dark teal for the cab. Now I'm starting to write the wheel function, laying out tread blocks as small boxes rotated around the wheel's axis.

Writing wheel geometry code...

Still working out the extrusion geometry... ribs at several z-positions with slightly scaled outlines, then side panel decals positioned on the pod's vertical faces.

Checking the facing direction of each decal plane so text reads correctly on both left and right sides of the vehicle, since the local axes flip depending on which side the panel faces.

Now placing the turret assembly on the cab roof: a lathed base, a housing box, twin barrels extending forward with muzzle brakes, and a sensor dome on top, checking clearance against the pod. Then positioning the roof light bar near the front edge.

For the cab itself, I'm switching to an extruded side-profile approach along the x-axis, defining a polygon outline in the z-y plane for the sloped windshield and roof, then adding a separate hood box in front, and merging the hood into the same profile outline to get a continuous front hull shape.

Now I'm computing a tilted visor plane for the windshield, finding the slope's tangent and normal vectors to position and orient a slightly offset panel that sits flush against the angled glass surface.

I'm laying out front details next: warm-white headlight boxes flanking the grille, a hazard-texture bumper plane, and a push-bar wedge extruded from a side profile sketch.

Then I'm placing exhaust stacks at the cab sides, sizing cylinders and caps so they clear the pod and wheels while sitting flush against the cab width, plus brackets for support.

Adding more surface details now: a glowing top hatch on the pod with a red ring and lock handles, amber edge lights along the pod's chamfered sides, and cyan underglow strips running along the chassis length. I'm also adding armored skirt panels between the wheels to protect the chassis underside.

Checking wheel positions to fit skirt panels without clipping: there's a usable gap between the axles where I can center a skirt panel, while another gap is already filled by overlapping wheels so no panel is needed there, and I'm computing where to place fuel tanks beneath the chassis as well.

Positioning the tank straps relative to the frame, then working out axle cylinders and differential housings along the wheel line, and now placing the rear tail lights and a textured door panel on the back face of the pod so it reads correctly from outside.

Adding mudflaps behind the rear wheels, then setting up helper functions for boxes and cylinders to streamline building the remaining parts.

I'm also planning texture decals for the model: a hazard-stripe pattern drawn with diagonal yellow and black polygons, and a visor-style HUD texture with a dark glass background, cyan scan lines, and arrow indicators, all rendered through SVG and applied as glowing decal planes.

Beyond that I'm sketching a logo plate with magenta trim and "KURO" lettering, a pod door design with a biohazard-style ring, wedge shapes, "SEALED" text and lock bolts, and a side panel with cargo warning text, a barcode, arrows, and kanji, then defining the dark steel and plate color palette to paint them all.
